name: json_schema_validate

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) document to validate against. The validator's primary target is [draft-07](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/json-schema-release-notes); newer drafts work for the keywords the underlying [pboettch/json-schema-validator](https://github.com/pboettch/json-schema-validator) supports.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The JSON value to validate. Pass a column of type `JSON`, a struct literal, or a string cast with `::JSON`.

returns: BOOLEAN — `TRUE` if the value conforms, `FALSE` otherwise.
description:
Validate a JSON value against a JSON Schema. Returns a plain `BOOLEAN`, so it composes naturally with `WHERE`, `CASE`, and `COUNT(*) FILTER (...)`.

This function does **not** return structured error detail — it answers conformance only. For a full per-keyword failure report, validate at the application layer with [ajv](https://ajv.js.org/) / [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/json_schema/) / [jsonschema](https://python-jsonschema.readthedocs.io/) and use this function as the coarse SQL gate.

examples.description: Filter a column on schema conformance

examples.code:
SELECT
  COUNT(*)                                                         AS total,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE     json_schema_validate(:schema, payload)) AS valid,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT json_schema_validate(:schema, payload)) AS invalid
FROM events;

name: json_schema_validate_schema

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: The candidate [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) document. Will be checked against the validator's meta-schema.

returns: BOOLEAN — `TRUE` if the schema is well-formed, `FALSE` otherwise.
description:
Lint a JSON Schema before applying it. Catches typos and structural mistakes that would otherwise cause every [`json_schema_validate`](#json_schema_validate) call to fail at runtime.

A reasonable habit: gate schema deployments through this function in CI, the same way you'd run a YAML or SQL linter.

examples.description: Find any malformed schemas in a registry table

name: json_schema_patch

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) document. Properties whose `default` keyword is set are the ones that contribute to the patch.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The (possibly incomplete) JSON value. Missing properties for which the schema declares a `default` will appear in the resulting patch.

returns: JSON — a [JSON Patch (RFC 6902)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6902) array of `add` operations that, when applied, fill in the missing defaults.
description:
Compute the [JSON Patch (RFC 6902)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6902) diff that would bring `json_data` into conformance with the `default` values declared by the schema. Returns the patch — does **not** apply it (use [`json_schema_update`](#json_schema_update) for the in-place variant).

Use the patch when you want to log or audit which fields were synthesized, or when you need to apply the same diff to multiple downstream representations of the document.

examples.description: Generate a patch for a partial document
Materialize patches alongside the original payload for auditing
examples.code:
SELECT
  payload,
  json_schema_patch(:schema, payload) AS defaults_patch
FROM events_raw;

name: json_schema_update

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) document. Properties with `default` declared are filled in where the input is missing them.

parameters.name: json_data
parameters.description: The JSON value to enrich. Existing fields are preserved; only missing properties with declared `default` values are added.

returns: JSON — the input value with missing defaults filled in.
description:
Apply the schema's `default` values inline. Equivalent to running [`json_schema_patch`](#json_schema_patch) and applying the resulting patch — but in a single function call you can use directly in a `SELECT` projection.

This is the function to reach for when you want enriched JSON, not a diff.

examples.description: Build a clean table with defaults applied
examples.code:
CREATE TABLE events_enriched AS
SELECT json_schema_update(:schema, payload) AS payload
FROM events_raw
WHERE json_schema_validate(:schema, payload);
